role: President of the European Law Students' Association (ELSA) at Zagreb, Croatian and European level
description: According to his official government CV, he chaired ELSA in Zagreb (1991), Croatia (1992) and Europe (1993) while studying law in Zagreb.

role: Official in the Directorate for Multilateral Affairs, the Office of the Deputy Minister and the Analysis Department
organization: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Croatia (Ministarstvo vanjskih poslova)
description: First posts in the Croatian diplomatic service, listed in his official CV.

role: Head of the Department for European Integration
organization: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Croatia
description: Headed the ministry's department dealing with Croatia's relations with and integration into the European Union.

role: Deputy Head of the Mission of the Republic of Croatia to the European Union
organization: Mission of the Republic of Croatia to the European Union, Brussels
description: Deputy head of Croatia's diplomatic mission to the EU in Brussels during the period of Croatia's candidacy.

role: Deputy Ambassador of the Republic of Croatia to France
organization: Embassy of the Republic of Croatia in Paris
description: Deputy head of the Croatian embassy in France (zamjenik veleposlanika).

organization: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and European Integration (MVEP)
description: State secretary in the government of Jadranka Kosor during the final phase of Croatia's EU accession negotiations.

role: Member of the Croatian Parliament (7th term), HDZ
description: Elected in December 2011 on the HDZ list in the VII constituency. Member of the Foreign Affairs, Judiciary, Environment and Nature Conservation, Interparliamentary Co-operation and European Integration committees and chair of the delegation to the Croatia–EU Joint Parliamentary Committee. From 16 March 2012 he was also an observer to the European Parliament; his parliamentary mandate was suspended on 1 July 2013, when he became an MEP.

role: Observer, then Member of the European Parliament (7th term), EPP group
description: Observer with the EPP group from April 2012 until Croatia's accession, then a full member from 1 July 2013 after the April 2013 European election. Member of the Committee on Budgets and of the delegation for relations with Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Montenegro and Kosovo; substitute on the Committee on Constitutional Affairs.

role: Member of the European Parliament (8th term), EPP group
description: Re-elected in May 2014 at the head of the HDZ-led list. Chair of the delegation to the EU–Ukraine Parliamentary Association Committee (from September 2014) and vice-chair of the Committee on Foreign Affairs; member of the committees on constitutional affairs, fisheries and budgets and of the Euronest delegation. He left the Parliament on becoming Prime Minister.

role: Member of the HDZ; member of the party's Central Committee (2011–2016)
description: Joined the HDZ in 2011, the year he entered parliament, and sat on its Central Committee until becoming party president.

role: President of the Croatian Democratic Union (predsjednik HDZ-a)
description: Took over the party at extraordinary internal elections in 2016, after criticising the then leader Tomislav Karamarko at a party assembly with the message that the party 'must not be hostage to the fate of one member' (Dnevnik Nova TV); re-elected for the terms beginning in 2020 and 2024, according to his official CV.

role: Prime Minister of the Republic of Croatia (predsjednik Vlade)
organization: Government of the Republic of Croatia (Vlada Republike Hrvatske)
description: Head of the 14th government (19 October 2016 – 23 July 2020), first with Most and from June 2017 with HNS; of the 15th government (23 July 2020 – 17 May 2024), with SDSS and other minority representatives among its supporters; and of the 16th government since 17 May 2024, with the Homeland Movement (DP), which holds three ministries. As of October 2026 only three ministers – Tomo Medved, Oleg Butković and Nina Obuljen Koržinek – have served throughout his ten years in office (Dnevnik Nova TV).
